title: Ritense bridges the Camunda cohort and Common Ground: Valtimo is open-source case management built on Camunda
content:
Ritense builds and supports Valtimo/GZAC, open-source low-code case management licensed EUPL-1.2 and built on Camunda. It is delivered as cloud, as a subscription and as downloadable open source, so the same product is available on three commercial footings.

That combination is why the research calls it the bridge between two otherwise separate parts of the corpus. The Camunda cohort is a group of leads whose process engine orchestrates work without holding a record of what each step decided; Common Ground is the Dutch municipal architecture. Valtimo sits in both, and the pairing has already been demonstrated in practice — BPMN inside Common Ground with Gemeente Utrecht.

The research goes further and says that if one firm validates the whole thesis, it is this one. A proof here would not be confined to a single stack: it would show that the Camunda gap is real and that closing it is acceptable inside a municipal architecture, which are the two claims much of the rest of the corpus rests on. The EUPL-1.2 licence also means an openly licensed record layer needs no licensing exception.
